notes: Two concurrent `hermes chat` REPLs in the SAME <staging>/cwd (driver start_session step; per-step {"session":1} targeting). Every phase anchors on a WORKING transition rather than a ready one: hermes mints a proc-<PID> pre-session per process that is born in ready and never enters working, so a ready-anchored birth would greedily match the placeholder and cascade. Assertions: (1) session 1 does an independent working→ready turn; (2) a DISTINCT session enters working (new_session:true proves it is not session 1) and completes its own turn; (3) session 1 is driven AGAIN while session 2 is alive, pinned same_session_as its first turn — proving its binding stayed stable and never flapped. Same-cwd is what makes this observable at all on the CLI surface: sessions.cwd is NULL for source='cli', and defaultLiveCWD's ambiguity guard counts DISTINCT cwds (LiveCWDsByCmdline returns a set of directories), so two processes in one directory still resolve a project binding and each session gets its own PID via claim-aware disambiguation. Budgets are sized for hermes' slow REPL boot plus the ~2s lazy INSERT of the sessions row. Observations: model is the shipped config default confirmed against live sessions rows; cost is priced by irrlicht's capacity table because hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under billing_mode='subscription_included'.
